newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Job creation vital for S.Africa future - business.
newsitem.headline: Job creation vital for S.Africa future - business.

text.p: Job creation is the most critical factor for South Africa's future, Business South Africa (BSA) chairman Hans Smith told a one-day summit of the Nedlac economic forum on Saturday.

"Nedlac, on every issue should ask the question...will the action we propose contribute to the creation of jobs," he told the second annual summit of the National Economic Development and Labour Council which groups business, labour and government.
The need to generate jobs on a massive scale was underscored by the fact that the unemployment rate was roughly 30 percent of the total labour force.
"It is estimated that the country's economy needs to grow at an annual average rate of at least six percent to absorb new entrants into the labour force," Smith said.

Job growth so far in South Africa has been negligible and employment targets envisaged in government's Growth, Employment and Redistribution (GEAR) plan released last June are unlikely to be met, analysts say.
South Africa's economy grew by a modest 3.1 percent in 1996.
Government's GEAR strategy envisages a growth rate of six percent per annum and 400,000 jobs per annum by the year 2000.
Smith underlined the need to create "micro enterprises" to tackle the chronic unemployment problem.
"The importance of the role of new black business and small business in the job creation process cannot be stressed enough."
Government this week announced a Presidential Jobs Summit to be held this year to thrash out an accord for employment and growth.
Labour Minister Tito Mboweni told Nedlac the summit should be an opportunity to promote economic development, growth and job creation without undermining labour security.
